title: Lifting morphisms between canonical formal glueing objects
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings and $\varphi:R\to S$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $t\in\mathbf N$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to R$, and $I=(f_i)_i$, and suppose the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is bijective. Let $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}(\varphi,f)$ be a functor with the canonical object components $S\otimes_R M,M_{f_i},c^M_{f_i},\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j}$ and map components $1\otimes h,h_{f_i}$, with bundled equalities and heterogeneous equalities of the actual structural and component maps as in [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], [def-weil-module-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. For any $R$-modules $M,N$ and any morphism $z:\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$ there exists an $R$-linear map $h:M\to N$ with $\mathrm{Can}(h)=z$. This asserts surjectivity only, not uniqueness or essential surjectivity.

proof.text: (Part (2): from now on $\varphi$ is flat and $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism. The complex.) For an $R$-module $N$ let $\alpha_N:N\to(N\otimes_RS)\times\prod_iN_{f_i}$, $n\mapsto(n\otimes1,(n/1)_i)$, and $\beta_N$ be the maps of [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-complex-exact], where $(N\otimes_RS)_{f_i}$ is identified with $N_{f_i}\otimes_RS$ by $c^N_{f_i}$ (the identification of that statement is $(x\otimes s)/f_i^e\leftrightarrow(x/f_i^e)\otimes s$, which is $c^N_{f_i}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps] (3)). By [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-complex-exact], $\alpha_N$ is injective and $\operatorname{Ker}\beta_N=\operatorname{Im}\alpha_N$. Concretely, a pair $(n',(n_i)_i)$ lies in $\operatorname{Ker}\beta_N$ iff (i) $c^N_{f_i}(n'/1)=n_i\otimes1$ for all $i$ and (ii) $n_i$ and $n_j$ have the same image in $N_{f_if_j}$ under the canonical maps $N_{f_i}\to N_{f_if_j}$, $x/f_i^e\mapsto f_j^ex/(f_if_j)^e$, and $N_{f_j}\to N_{f_if_j}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], for all $i,j$.

proof.text: (Part (2): a lemma on iterated localizations.) Let $N$ be an $R$-module, $f,g\in R$, $x,y\in N$, $a,b\ge0$, and suppose $\sigma^N_{f,g}((x/f^a)/1)=(y/g^b)/1$ in $(N_g)_f$. Then $x/f^a$ and $y/g^b$ have the same image in $N_{fg}$. Indeed $\sigma^N_{f,g}((x/f^a)/1)=(x/1)/f^a$ (step 1), so $(x/1)/f^a=(y/g^b)/1$ in $(N_g)_f$: there is $c\ge0$ with $f^c\big(x/1-f^a\cdot y/g^b\big)=0$ in $N_g$, i.e. $(f^cg^bx-f^{c+a}y)/g^b=0$, so there is $d\ge0$ with $g^d(f^cg^bx-f^{a+c}y)=0$ in $N$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. The images of $x/f^a$ and $y/g^b$ in $N_{fg}$ are $g^ax/(fg)^a$ and $f^by/(fg)^b$ (canonical maps of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]); their difference is $z/(fg)^{a+b}$ with $z=f^bg^{a+b}x-f^{a+b}g^ay=f^bg^a(g^bx-f^ay)$, and $(fg)^{c+d}z=f^{b+d}g^{a+c}\cdot g^d(f^cg^bx-f^{a+c}y)=0$. Hence the difference is $0$ in $N_{fg}$.

proof.text: (Part (2): $\mathrm{Can}$ is full.) Let $(u',(u_i)_i):\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$ be a morphism of $\mathrm{Glue}$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]: $u'$ is $S$-linear, the $u_i:M_{f_i}\to N_{f_i}$ are $R$-linear, $c^N_{f_i}\circ u'_{f_i}=(u_i\otimes_RS)\circ c^M_{f_i}$ and $\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}\circ(u_i)_{f_j}=(u_j)_{f_i}\circ\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j}$. Let $m\in M$, $n'=u'(m\otimes1)$, $n_i=u_i(m/1)$. Applying the first relation to $(m\otimes1)/1$ gives $c^N_{f_i}(n'/1)=(u_i\otimes_RS)((m/1)\otimes1)=n_i\otimes1$ (formula for $c$, step 1), which is (i) of step 3. Applying the second to $(m/1)/1$ gives $\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}(n_i/1)=(u_j)_{f_i}((m/1)/1)=n_j/1$; writing $n_i=x/f_i^a$, $n_j=y/f_j^b$, step 4 shows that $n_i$ and $n_j$ have the same image in $N_{f_if_j}$, which is (ii). So $(n',(n_i))\in\operatorname{Ker}\beta_N=\operatorname{Im}\alpha_N$, and by injectivity of $\alpha_N$ there is exactly one $u(m)\in N$ with $u(m)\otimes1=u'(m\otimes1)$ and $u(m)/1=u_i(m/1)$ for all $i$ (step 3). The map $u$ is $R$-linear: $\alpha_N(u(m_1)+r\,u(m_2))$ and $\alpha_N(u(m_1+rm_2))$ are both $(u'((m_1+rm_2)\otimes1),(u_i((m_1+rm_2)/1))_i)$, as $u'$, $u_i$, $\alpha_N$ are $R$-linear. Now $u\otimes_RS$ and $u'$ are $S$-linear and agree on the elements $m\otimes1$, which generate $M\otimes_RS$ over $S$ [def-weil-module-base-change], so $u\otimes_RS=u'$; and $u_{f_i}$, $u_i$ are $R$-linear maps into $N_{f_i}$, on which $f_i$ acts bijectively [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], agreeing on the elements $m/1$, so they agree on $m/f_i^e$ (both send it to the unique $z$ with $f_i^ez=u(m)/1$). Hence $(u',(u_i))=\mathrm{Can}(u)$; with step 5, $\mathrm{Can}$ is fully faithful.

theorem canonical_map_surjective {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R)
    (Can : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R ⥤ Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f)
    (hobj : (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        (Can.obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, (Can.obj M).M i =
          ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin t,
          HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))))
    (hmap : (∀ (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (h : M ⟶ N),
        HEq (Can.map h).prime (extendMap φ h.hom) ∧
        ∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.map h).chart i) (localMap (f i) h.hom)))
    (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap ((Ideal.span (Set.range f)).map φ) φ Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) :
    Function.Surjective (Can.map : (M ⟶ N) → (Can.obj M ⟶ Can.obj N))
